q1.answer: No. ADR013 (use node-fetch) is explicitly marked superseded and says it 'no longer applies', replaced by ADR014. ADR014 says frontend plugins and packages should prefer to use fetchApiRef (which NotificationsClient does via the injected fetchApi), while Node.js/backend code should use native fetch.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires all fetch/XMLHttpRequest calls in tests to be mocked using msw. Rather than stating exactly 'two avoided things' in those words, it frames the problem as every test having its own ad-hoc mocking implementation (inconsistency across unit/e2e tests) and tests directly mocking fetch/XHR itself; msw avoids both by giving a single, express-style, shared way to intercept requests.

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly added a 'children' prop to every component (even when not wanted) and that Generic Type parameters were not supported on children. It notes React.FC was removed from Facebook's Create React App TypeScript template because it was found to be an unnecessary feature with next to no benefits and a few downsides (see the linked create-react-app PR #8177).

q4.answer: The alternative is Moment.js. ADR010 gives two reasons it's being retired: it's affected by large bundle sizes, and it has mutable state issues (plus the Moment.js project itself is being sunset/recommends alternatives).

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way down to the package root src/index.ts. It was specifically meant to make it easy to answer 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' / 'What is exported from this directory?'

q6.answer: No, they are not part of the public API. ADR004's rule is that a symbol is only publicly exported if it can be traced through an unbroken chain of index files up to src/index.ts; since there is no src/utils/index.ts re-exporting them and src/index.ts never mentions them, the chain is broken, so by the rule they are implicitly not exported even though nothing explicitly marks them private.

q7.answer: ADR011 says the x-react package is for shared widgets, hooks and similar code that both the plugin itself (x) and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a notifications-react package, other third-party frontend plugins would have to need to reuse its components/hooks directly, which currently isn't the case (it's all internal to the single package).

q8.answer: The one exception ADR003 allows is React.lazy() modules, which require a default export. The workaround it gives for avoiding even that is to wrap the lazy import with React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component }))), converting a named export into the required default at the call site.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the loader/component option pattern. Its Consequences section says the pattern will be applied to update APIs in the new @backstage/frontend-* packages, but explicitly states they will NOT update any existing APIs in the old frontend system (@backstage/core-* packages) — so pre-existing code like the dev app, which predates/uses the old system's style, will not be retrofitted.
